divergences.ours: Edge-axis zero-guard yields a finite matrix when a size-0 edge is present.
divergences.reason: Deliberate zero-guard (laplacian.rs). Only the default sparse=True path agrees; sparse=False diverges NaN-vs-finite.
divergences.xgi: np.diag(1/De) with De=0 gives inf, then 0*inf=nan: an all-NaN matrix. With an ONLY-empty-edge graph xgi raises ValueError instead.

divergences.ours: Missing-id messages quote str ids via repr(): "Edge 'x' not in the hypergraph", "'x' is not in the network".
divergences.reason: The PyO3 binding builds the message from edge.repr() before the core call, so MembershipError's XGI-matching arms are unreachable. str ids only; ints/floats/tuples/bytes match. State machinery is conformant.
divergences.xgi: Plain f-string interpolation: "Edge x not in the hypergraph", "ID x not found".

divergences.ours: Auto-id counter bumps whenever the canonicalized key parses as u64, so idx='5' or '007' bumps.
divergences.reason: PyIdMap canonicalizes str and int to the same core String key, so the core cannot make XGI's isinstance(idx, int) distinction.
divergences.xgi: Bumps only for a real Python int; idx='5' leaves the counter at 0.

divergences.ours: No bump for idx=5.0 or idx=True; the next auto id is 0.
divergences.reason: Same mechanism as D3 in the opposite direction: canonical(5.0)/canonical(True) never produce a u64-parsable key.
divergences.xgi: Bumps when float.is_integer(), and for bool (an int subclass): next auto id 6 / 2.

divergences.ours: Exact insertion order, byte-stable across every PYTHONHASHSEED.
divergences.reason: Task 2's owner-upgrade gave the Di core insertion order; it leaks into a Python list here. Directed only — the undirected control is identical at every seed. tail/head/dimembers/memberships are sets on both and must NOT be reported.
divergences.xgi: Python set-iteration order, varying with the hash seed.

divergences.api: Hypergraph/DiHypergraph/SimplicialComplex add_node, add_nodes_from, add_edge, add_edges_from, add_simplex — a None id
divergences.ours: None is stringified to the core key "None" and silently accepted as a node.
divergences.reason: Missing shape validation at the binding boundary (the Phase-7 obligation D7 assigns to the binding). Reproduces on 6 entry points across all three classes. idx=None correctly means auto-assign on both.
divergences.xgi: IDDict.__setitem__ raises XGIError('None cannot be a node or edge'); SC.add_simplex raises ValueError.

divergences.ours: Deletes incident edges AND cleans surviving nodes' reverse index: degree 0, isolates reported, a second removal succeeds.
divergences.reason: Undirected remove_node is fully conformant across the 2x2 flag matrix; only the directed strong path diverges.
divergences.xgi: dihypergraph.py:417-420 deletes _edge without reverse-index cleanup: surviving nodes keep dangling refs, degree/memberships/dimemberships/isolates disagree, and a second removal raises IDNotFound.

divergences.api: Hypergraph.add_node_to_edge / DiHypergraph.add_node_to_edge with a numeric edge id
divergences.ours: Bumps the auto-id counter, so a following auto add_edge gets id 6 (edges ['5','6']).
divergences.reason: Deliberate extension of the D3/D4 bump rule to close XGI's collision class. Non-numeric ids agree; the gap widens with larger ids (['0','1','100'] vs ['100','101','102']).
divergences.xgi: Never touches the counter (edges ['0','5']); a later auto id can silently overwrite the edge.

divergences.ours: Raises XGIError("Frozen higher-order network can't be modified").
divergences.reason: XGI's freeze monkey-patches a fixed method list with omissions; ours is real state checked uniformly. Exactly these three ops, no more: a 21-op frozen-mutator sweep agrees everywhere else.
divergences.xgi: Succeeds silently and mutates the frozen network.

divergences.api: Hypergraph.copy / DiHypergraph.copy of a frozen graph
divergences.ours: The copy is frozen (is_frozen True) and refuses add_edge.
divergences.reason: XGI's freeze is per-instance method swizzling that a fresh copy never inherits; ours is struct data carried by copy(). is_frozen is a property (not a method) on both.
divergences.xgi: The copy is mutable (is_frozen False) and accepts add_edge.

divergences.ours: No exception: creates edge 0 with tail={'a'}, head={'b'}, dropping the rest.
divergences.reason: The binding's shape check is get_item(0)/get_item(1), which any str satisfies; XGI uses isinstance(members,(tuple,list)). Length-conditional: 'a' and '' do raise. Same shape-check also gives bytes -> TypeError (xgi XGIError) and [[1]] -> XGIError (xgi IndexError).
divergences.xgi: XGIError('Directed edge must be a list or tuple!').

divergences.ours: Honours idx=0, '', False, 0.0 literally, creating an edge with that id and type.
divergences.reason: The binding branches on whether the kwarg was supplied, never on truthiness. The divergence needs id 0 FREE while the uid counter has moved past it — e.g. add_simplex(m0, idx=5) first, then idx=0/''/False/0.0 all diverge identically (xgi auto-assigns 6, ours honours the literal id). If id 0 is occupied instead (e.g. an unadorned auto-id add_simplex first), xgi's `if idx in self._edge` guard fires before the truthiness check for 0/False/0.0 — both refuse with a uid-exists warning, matching ours — and only idx='' still diverges.
divergences.xgi: `next(_edge_uid) if not idx else idx` — falsy idx is ignored and the next uid is auto-assigned.

divergences.api: is_uniform(H) when, after discarding singleton (size-1) edges, the only remaining edge size is 0
divergences.ours: Returns False (falsy) — usize cannot represent -1.
divergences.reason: Oracle-verified deviation (properties.rs:64-79, which documents this exact case). Measured via single add_edge calls per fixture (add_edges_from would hit D32's first-position IndexError on an all-empty edge list): only-empty, empty+size-1, and two-empty edges all diverge (ours False, xgi -1); empty+size-2 and empty+size-3 AGREE (both False), since the non-singleton size set then has 2 elements on both sides.
divergences.xgi: Discards singleton edges first (same unique_edge_sizes()-minus-{1} rule as ours); returns int -1 (TRUTHY) only when what remains is exactly {0}. `if is_uniform(H):` takes the branch under xgi and not under us in that case.

divergences.api: max_edge_order(H) when at least one edge exists and the largest is size 0
divergences.ours: Returns None, so `max_edge_order(H) + 1` raises TypeError.
divergences.reason: Same usize/-1 unrepresentability as REV-1. Tightly bounded: the true no-edges-with-nodes case is 0 on both, and empty+size-3 is 2 on both.
divergences.xgi: Returns int -1, so the same expression yields 0.

divergences.api: sunflower(l, c, m) with m == c
divergences.ours: Bounded `for p in 0..l`: returns c nodes and l parallel edges in milliseconds.
divergences.reason: Deliberate Power-of-10 rule 2 bounded-loop port. Verified: `timeout 5` on xgi exits 124; ours exits 0.
divergences.xgi: simple.py:114 `while start_label + (m-c) <= c + (m-c)*l` becomes `while c <= c`: infinite loop, process must be killed.

divergences.ours: Empty `start..=(max_order+1)` range: returns 4 nodes, 0 edges, no exception.
divergences.reason: The Rust port has no equivalent assertion. A caller relying on the call to validate max_order sees success-with-wrong-result instead of a raise.
divergences.xgi: classic.py:264 asserts end >= start unconditionally: bare AssertionError.

divergences.ours: Relabeled nodes and edges carry no provenance attribute (all attrs {}).
divergences.reason: hypergraph.rs:1625-1628 relabel_to_integers is a private duplicate of the standalone convert_labels_to_integers minus the label attribute. The standalone free function is unaffected.
divergences.xgi: convert_labels_to_integers(label_attribute='label') stamps {'label': <pre-relabel id>} on every node and edge.

divergences.ours: Deterministic two-column bipartite_layout; seed accepted for signature parity and ignored (seed 0 and seed 1 give identical positions).
divergences.reason: Declared deviation (layout.rs:11-12, 75-78). The ported test only asserts same-seed self-consistency, which a constant function satisfies trivially — no test catches this.
divergences.xgi: Seeded force-directed layout: node 1 at (-0.059, 1.0) for seed=0 vs (-0.822, 0.560) for seed=1.

divergences.ours: The mutated edge moves to the END of edge iteration order (['e1','e2','e0']).
divergences.reason: The core has no edge_attrs_mut, so assign_attr (dihypergraph.rs:1092-1118) removes and re-adds the edge; composing that with D5's insertion-order upgrade made it observable. Node-attr mutation is unaffected.
divergences.xgi: Order is unchanged (['e0','e1','e2']).

divergences.api: attribute VALUE and KEY channel on add_node / add_edge / set_node_attributes / set_edge_attributes (all classes)
divergences.ours: serde_json-typed: a set or custom object raises TypeError('... is not JSON-serializable'); a tuple round-trips as a list; a non-str key is coerced to str (1 -> '1'); keys come back sorted (BTreeMap).
divergences.reason: Declared deviation (pyid.rs:171-213). Root cause shared with D31; reachable from every ordinary attribute entry point, not just merge_duplicate_edges.
divergences.xgi: Stores arbitrary Python objects verbatim; tuple stays tuple; int keys stay int; insertion order preserved.

divergences.ours: Materialized list: len() works, re-iterable.
divergences.reason: Documented deviation (utils.rs:59-61). No ported test checks the return type or re-iteration.
divergences.xgi: itertools.chain: len() raises TypeError, single-use (second list() is empty).

divergences.ours: Materialized list[set]; len() works; next() raises TypeError ('list' is not an iterator).

divergences.xgi: Generator of sets; len() raises.

divergences.api: H.nodes.degree / H.edges.order and other Stat views — .asdict() / .aslist()
divergences.ours: The id SET is captured once at getter-invocation time. Values for those ids recompute live, but any node or edge added afterwards never appears.

divergences.xgi: Lazy view over the live node/edge set: a node added after the getter call shows up in asdict().

divergences.ours: Return snapshot PyDict copies: writes and deletes hit a throwaway dict; `del H._node['test']` leaves the node in place and num_nodes unchanged; a later `del H._net_attr['test']` raises KeyError.
divergences.reason: Already recorded in exclusions.toml (algorithms/test_properties.py::test_equal, utils/test_utilities.py::test_iddict) but with no symbol-keyed entry a compat lookup can reach. Fixing needs a mutable-mapping proxy.

divergences.xgi: -> True; the dispatch machinery caches the Stat object.

divergences.ours: Remainder stubs dropped and within-edge picks deduplicated for bounded termination, so both the EDGE COUNT and the realised degree sequence differ: k={i:3 for i in range(12)}, seed 42 gives 11 edges with degrees [1,2,3x10].
divergences.reason: Documented core deviation (uniform.rs); exact parity is unattainable under the bounded-loop policy. Re-verified 2026-07-30 against xgi 0.10.2 — the original wording ('close to but not bit-exact') understated it by omitting the edge-count difference.
divergences.xgi: Stub-matching that warns when k is unrealizable; the same input gives 12 edges with degrees [3]x12, hitting k exactly and emitting no warning.

divergences.reason: Same JSON-typed channel as D23. rename='first'/'tuple'/'new' and merge_rule='first'/'intersection' are conformant.
divergences.xgi: Merged attr is a Python set: {'color': {'red','blue'}}.

divergences.ours: Silently discarded: no exception, no warning, and the attribute is absent on the next read.

divergences.api: Hypergraph.cleanup() and Hypergraph.cleanup(in_place=True) — the DEFAULT path

ARITY CORRECTED 2026-07-30: the first draft named in_place=False, which is the one path that agrees; the divergence is on the default path everyone calls.

divergences.api: class MyGraph(hypergraph_rs.Hypergraph) — subclassing any core class
divergences.ours: TypeError: type 'hypergraph_rs.Hypergraph' is not an acceptable base type; Py_TPFLAGS_BASETYPE is False.
divergences.reason: PyO3 classes are not subclassable unless declared #[pyclass(subclass)]. Import-fatal at class-definition time, so a consumer that subclasses cannot even load. Found during the method-layer sweep, absent from the 34-entry register.
divergences.xgi: Subclasses normally; Py_TPFLAGS_BASETYPE is True.

divergences.ours: draw_nodes and draw_hyperedges are literal aliases of draw (`_require_mpl(lambda *a, **k: draw(*a, **k))`): all three render the whole scene identically (measured on the same fixture, each on its own Axes: 0 patches, 4 lines) and return a bare `Axes`. `ax, collections = hrs.draw(H)` raises `TypeError: cannot unpack non-iterable Axes object`. All three carry the wrapper's `(*args, **kwargs)` signature — draw_nodes/draw_hyperedges expose none of their own per-element styling kwargs.
divergences.reason: Measured with matplotlib installed in this repo's .venv against xgi 0.10.2, closing evidence-doc gap 2 (docs/superpowers/specs/evidence/2026-07-30-divergence-register-measurement.md §7): 'not re-run (matplotlib), so not in the TOML; verify then add as a D37 sibling.' divergences.xgi: Three distinct functions. `draw` returns `(ax, (node_collection, dyad_collection, edge_collection))`; `draw_nodes` returns `(ax, node_collection)` and renders only nodes; `draw_hyperedges` returns `(ax, (dyad_collection, edge_collection))` and renders only dyads/hyperedges — each with its own 10-15 styling kwargs (node_fc, node_size, dyad_color, edge_fc, ...).

partial_symbols.reason: Random-sampling assortativity path awaits the Phase-4 rand_pcg pin (module doc, algorithms.rs). Only exact=True is ported. xgi's exact=False path returns a Python float when the sampled degree pairs have variance (measured: -0.647 on a varied-degree fixture) but returns the literal int 0, not a float, when corrcoef is NaN from zero variance — the uniform-triangle fixture this entry's own test uses hits exactly that path, with a 'RuntimeWarning: invalid value encountered in divide'. Verified against real xgi 0.10.2.
partial_symbols.trigger: exact=False (the default) — any kind/num_samples/seed; the bare call degree_assortativity(H) already hits this

partial_symbols.reason: The in_degree getter constructs DiStat with both degree_source and edge_source None, so __call__'s fallback branch always raises. xgi re-dispatches and returns a filtered/re-parametrized Stat instead. Not covered by any ported test (untested per the T1 recon) and not in exclusions.toml.
partial_symbols.trigger: Invoking the Stat as a function at all — D.nodes.in_degree(...) or even D.nodes.in_degree() with zero arguments. The bare property access D.nodes.in_degree (no call) does not raise.

partial_symbols.reason: Identical root cause and fix to in_degree: the out_degree getter also constructs DiStat with both sources None. xgi returns a valid re-parametrized Stat; ours raises unconditionally on call.
partial_symbols.trigger: Invoking the Stat as a function at all, including zero-arg D.nodes.out_degree().

partial_symbols.reason: PyEdgeStat's Attr arm is the one EdgeStatKind that never got a re-parametrization branch (contrast PyNodeStat::Attr at stats.rs:280-293, which does re-parametrize and does not raise for the identical H.nodes.attrs(key)() shape). xgi returns a re-dispatched Stat, not an error.
partial_symbols.trigger: Re-invoking the EdgeStat returned by H.edges.attrs(key) with zero arguments — H.edges.attrs('color')(). A str positional instead raises TypeError from PyO3 extraction before the Attr arm is reached. Only the Attr kind raises; Size/Order re-parametrize fine on the same __call__.

partial_symbols.reason: hypergraph-rs makes matplotlib an optional `mpl` extra, so this symbol imports and raises only at call time. xgi 0.10.2 hard-depends on matplotlib (Requires-Dist: matplotlib>=3.4), so the same environment cannot host xgi at all. This entry records the raise-on-missing-matplotlib path only — it is NOT the only divergence: with matplotlib present, the call site itself diverges too (draw returns a bare Axes where xgi returns a tuple; see D39, compat/divergences.toml).
partial_symbols.trigger: any call in an environment without matplotlib installed
